subject: design-technology
title: Metals
welcome_lead: Ferrous, non-ferrous and what they're used.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: ferrous metals, non-ferrous metals, alloys.
final_note: Metals are strong, conductive and recyclable.

concepts.def: Metal with no iron — won't rust.
Ferrous alloy of iron and carbon.

walkthroughs.body_html: Ferrous metals contain iron — steel, cast iron, mild steel. They are strong but rust when exposed to water and oxygen. Magnets stick to them.
Non-ferrous metals contain no iron — aluminium, copper, brass, gold. They don't rust. Aluminium is light (planes, cans). Copper conducts electricity well (wires).
An alloy is a mix of metals. Brass = copper + zinc. Bronze = copper + tin. Stainless steel = steel + chromium (won't rust).

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a jig in manufacturing?
options: To hold the workpiece very tightly so it does not move.
To guide a tool and ensure consistent, accurate repeated operations.

mcqs.q: Why can thermoplastics be recycled but thermosets cannot?
options: Thermoplastics soften when heated and can be remoulded; thermosets have cross-links that lock the shape permanently.
Thermosets are too dangerous to recycle.
Thermoplastics are cheaper, so it is worth recycling them.
